ledger.note: 1282: Fong founds Mueang Pua. The infobox reads 'Pua founded 1282' and 'Fong (1282-1302, first)', with Phukha's rule 1269-1337 and the kingdom 'established in the 13th century'. Phayao sent an army to take Pua in 1263 and held it to 1323, so the independence is nominal at first.

region.text: the former Phayao subject mueangs along the upper Yom River (read as Pong and Chiang Muan, the circle the phayao-kingdom dossier uses)

ledger.note: 1338: Nan takes Phayao's eastern cities. 'In 1338, Phanong and Khamfu of Lan Na coordinated an attack to sack the city of Phayao'; Khamfu kept the loot, and after 1338 Nan held 'the former Phayao subject mueangs along the upper Yom River'. The region is the phayao-kingdom dossier's reading.

1368: Nan is founded as the capital. The Nan Chronicle has the court 'shift gradually south to found Nan in 1368' (infobox 'Nan (1368-1448)'), after Pua (1282-1359) and Phu Phiang Chae Haeng (1359-1368).

region.text: the Nan River basin: Mueang Pua, Mueang Nan and the upper Nan with the salt wells at Bo Mang

ledger.note: 1399: Phrae conquers Nan. 'The two ruling brothers of Phrae, Then and Ounmueang, conquered Nan and killed Srichanta.' Then ruled about six months.

region.text: the Nan River basin: Mueang Pua, Mueang Nan and the upper Nan with the salt wells at Bo Mang

ledger.note: 1400: Hung retakes the Nan throne. Ounmueang was captured in 1400 by Hung, who had Sukhothai's backing.

ledger.note: 1449: Tilokaraj of Lan Na conquers Nan. 'Tilokaraj marched from Mueang Lo through Mueang Pong and Mueang Khuan before bombarding Nan with artillery fire'; Intakaenthao fled to Chaliang. Phasaeng ruled as Tilokaraj's vassal until 1459 and 'Nan was annexed into Lan Na in 1461'; the infobox dates the state to 1448.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by se-01-d ('nan-kingdom' in phayao-kingdom's 1338 loss) and se-01-e. One page opened (budget 2-5, thin). Not settled: (1) the page runs the state from the 13th century to 1449 (infobox 1448); the later Nan (Burmese rule 1558-1788, Thonburi vassal 1775, Siamese vassal to 1931) is not on this page and has no dossier (thonburi-kingdom and the Burma dossier carry counterpart 'nan'; suggested slug nan, group se-01-x or a later batch); (2) Phayao ruled Pua 1263-1323 (infobox), so the independence 1282-1323 is nominal; (3) the lan-na-kingdom dossier has no event for the 1449 conquest or the 1461 annexation, and the phayao-kingdom 1338 loss uses a 20 km circle that is the only extent given for the Yom mueangs; (4) the page's succession dates are inconsistent: 1434 or 1431 or 1484 for the capture by Ayutthaya's ally, Phasaeng's reign 1450-1461 (infobox) or to 1459 (text); (5) Mueang Phrae has no dossier (suggested slug phrae) (Phrae was Sukhothai's tributary 1294-1298 in sukhothai-kingdom); (6) capital coordinates are approximate.
